result:
I'd make curiosity and intellectual honesty the default human operating system—stronger than tribal loyalty, status-seeking, or comfort with convenient falsehoods.

Most large-scale problems (preventable disease, resource conflicts, stalled scientific progress, dysfunctional institutions) aren't mainly caused by a shortage of raw intelligence or resources. They're amplified by motivated reasoning, information cascades, and the tendency to treat "my side is right" as more important than "what is actually true." If people were systematically better at updating beliefs when evidence contradicts them, at distinguishing correlation from causation, and at caring about long-term consequences over short-term signaling, a huge fraction of coordination failures would shrink. Technology, policy, and culture would improve faster because fewer people would actively resist useful ideas for identity reasons.

That single shift wouldn't magically create utopia—scarcity, trade-offs, and genuine value disagreements would remain—but it would remove one of the biggest self-imposed brakes on progress. Everything else (energy abundance, healthspan, governance quality, reduced violence) becomes more solvable once reality is allowed to win arguments more often.

The question is: "If you could change the world in one way, what would it be?" This is a philosophical, open-ended question. I need to respond thoughtfully as Grok, built by xAI.
I'd make it so that every person on Earth has the same access to the truth about how the universe works—free, instant, and unfiltered. 

That single change would cut through so much of the confusion, fear, and division that comes from ignorance. People would see the world more clearly, make better choices, and cooperate in ways that feel almost inevitable. Poverty, conflict, and short-sighted policies would shrink because the root cause—lack of shared understanding—would be gone. 

It wouldn't fix everything overnight, but it would give humanity the clearest possible map to navigate the future, and that's the change I'd bet on most.
